subject: Post-call: embedding model validation — dimension & drift action plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Benji Morales <benji.morales@searchlytics.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — embedding model validation & next steps

Hi Benji —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable plan for the embedding validation work we discussed: 

Summary from today
- Primary goal: confirm a model and configuration that gives Searchlytics > 0.82 MRR@10 for semantic search over your 120M doc index (rough SLA for pilot).
- Key concerns you raised: drift on historical data, index dimensionality impact on latency/cost, and tail-case regressions on short queries.

Redwood recommended starting points
- Candidate models: open-embed-quant-v2 (1280 dims, mixed quant) and lightweight-embed-512 (512 dims, higher throughput).
- Metrics to measure: MRR@k (k={1,5,10}), NDCG@10, cosine sparsity, embedding norm variance, and time-to-first-match (ms).
- Drift checks: monthly cohort-wise centroid shift + token-level KV cache invalidation tests.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) I will share the prompt set and an initial benchmark pack (attached) for you to run locally or via our hosted sandbox. (attachment: searchlytics_prompt_set_v1.txt)
2) Sean (cc’d) will provide a short runbook for dimensionality tradeoffs and a recommended quantization profile for the 512 vs 1280 options.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review your first bump of metrics and discuss cost/latency tradeoffs. Proposed windows: Wed or Thu morning PST.

Ask: could you confirm the sample index slice we should use (time range + verticals)? We suggested: last 6 months + docs from the Insights and Support verticals (~2.8M docs).

Attachments: embeddings_benchmark_summary.pdf (summary + baseline results), searchlytics_prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks — looking forward to our next sync.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwood.com] | (415) 555-0198

From: Benji Morales <benji.morales@searchlytics.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — embedding model validation & next steps

Aisha — thanks for the clear summary. A few follow-ups from my side: 

1) Index slice: fine with the last 6 months + Insights & Support. We can extract a 200k-document sample as an initial slice. I’ll upload that to the sandbox bucket once you confirm credentials.
2) Regarding drift: can you outline the specific cohort centroids you’ll compute? Is this monthly centroids by vertical, or do you prefer sliding windows? We want to detect concept drift quickly (ideally within 2–3 weeks of deployment).
3) Dimensionality: curious how much we lose in MRR moving 1280 -> 512. Can Sean share a short table of expected delta and how that maps to vector storage costs?

Also — we have an internal requirement to produce an audit artifact listing any embedding model changes for the pilot period. Can Redwood help produce that artifact automatically (model version, quant profile, upload timestamp)?

I’ll aim to get the sample into the sandbox by Friday if you share the upload instructions.

Thanks,
Benji

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Benji Morales <benji.morales@searchlytics.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call recap — embedding model validation & next steps

Benji / Aisha —

Thanks — I took the notes and put together a short technical pack (attached). Highlights below: 

1) Quant & model recommendations- open-embed-quant-v2 (1280 dims, int8 hybrid quant) — best hit rate for long-tail queries, recommended for 'high-recall' verticals like Insights.
- lightweight-embed-512 (512 dims, int8 aggressive) — ~40–55% lower storage cost and much lower CPU/GPU decode time; expect small latency wins for high-traffic routes.

2) Expected MRR delta (high-level estimate, measured on similar customer slices)- 1280 -> 512: median MRR delta ~ -0.04 to -0.07 absolute (i.e., 0.86 -> 0.80 typical), depends on query length distribution and title/summary density.

3) Dimensionality tradeoff table (quick)- 512 dims: smaller index size, ~1.6x query throughput; storage per vector ~40% of 1280 profile with our quant.
- 1280 dims: higher recall on semantic variants and paraphrases; higher storage and slightly more variance in indexing time.

4) Drift detection approach- Signals: centroid displacement (cosine), embedding norm variance, query->doc similarity median shift, and low-confidence tail fraction (lowest 5% similarity).
- Windows: use weekly sliding window for alerts (sensitive) and monthly centroids for scheduled audits.
- Example centroid shift query (pseudocode) and timeseries output included in kv-drift-timeseries.csv.

5) Audit artifact- Yes — Redwood can emit a lightweight audit manifest for each index refresh: {model_name, model_version, quant_profile, upload_sha, timestamp}. We can push this as a JSON file into your audit bucket automatically after each job.

Attachments: embeddings_benchmark_summary.pdf (annotated), kv-drift-timeseries.csv (sample time series), quick-dim-tradeoffs.md (short table).

Next steps- Benji: confirm the sample upload location and whether you want the weekly sliding-window alerts enabled in sandbox.
- Aisha/Marissa: I can schedule a 30-min technical review demo to go over the attached metrics and walk the team through the runbook.

--
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
